rationale: Operator's ask was that the system learn more about him as he uses it so it can be tailored, not that it become a study app. Kiwi Learning's transferable part is the maths: a belief with a confidence that rises on confirming evidence, falls on contradicting evidence, and decays toward uncertainty when nothing reconfirms it. Applied to context_entries that gives Frodo a profile that is honest about what it actually still knows.

statement: validate-ui.mjs resolves the global stylesheet by the hardcoded basename globals.css, producing a false UI-7 failure and silently skipping UI-4

options.choice: extract the token layer into src/styles/globals.css and report the checker limitation upstream

options.choice: leave tokens in index.css and mark UI-4/UI-7 unmeasured
options.consequence: a second permanent blind spot alongside DR-004, and a 5223-line stylesheet QF-7 already objects to

choice: extract the token layer into src/styles/globals.css and report the checker limitation upstream
rationale: heyscottybro had three prefers-reduced-motion blocks the whole time; UI-7 was reported failing purely because the file was named index.css. Worse, validate-ui.mjs line 129 only runs the UI-4 border-token loop over files basenamed globals.css, so UI-4 was never checked on this repo and its green was meaningless. Extracting the :root and .admin-shell token scopes into styles/globals.css is what QF-7 asks for independently, so the fix is real rather than a rename to satisfy a grep. Upstream: the checker should resolve the global stylesheet from the entry import graph, not a basename.

Fonts: Roboto Slab (display) + system SF (body).

statement: Habits get a "Missed it" action: a day a habit won't get done is crossed out, not left overdue.
choice: accountability_state schema 2 adds misses[{id,trackerId,date,at}]. A miss is never a log: not done, no streak, no work-log mirror. dueHabits counts the next due date from the latest log OR miss, so a daily habit returns tomorrow and an every-N habit rolls on from the missed day. Missing a day already logged is refused; logging a missed day clears the miss. Undo everywhere. Agents: log_habit {missed: true|false}.
rationale: Scott, 2026-09-15: 'add in a missed it button to cross out any habits that won't get done'. Schema bump (not an optional field on v1) so an older build refuses the blob instead of silently dropping misses on save (QF-3).

Old /admin/recipes and ?tab=food links land on Life. Money › Receipts stays (it is a finance tool). rationale: Scott, 2026-09-16: 'delete smoke all together complete purge'.

statement: Orbit (the personal CRM) becomes heyScottyBro's People space, on Supabase, shared with the local Orbit app.
choice: People space at /admin/people (sidebar, command palette). Orbit's own UI runs in a shadow root with its own router (basename /admin/people), restyled via people-orbit.css token mapping; its code is a read-only copy in orbit/ made by scripts/sync-orbit.mjs from the Orbit repo. Data lives in orbit_people / orbit_events / orbit_settings (one row per record, doc jsonb, RLS owner-only); every request's changes are written by one orbit_apply call (security definer, auth.uid()). api/orbit.js serves Orbit's API behind the caller's Supabase session (vercel.json rewrites /api/orbit/* to it; api/briefing.js, an exact copy of api/chat.js, was removed to stay within the Hobby plan's 12 functions). The local Orbit server uses the same rows (ORBIT_BACKEND=supabase, Orbit DR-103..105). Frodo gets read-only people and people_events collections; people are added or changed only through Orbit (its Interview agent logs to agent_actions as agent_id orbit). Local data (70 people, 64 events) moved once; Orbit's data/ kept as backup.
rationale: Scott, 2026-09-17: 'put orbit into the site', choosing a People space inside heyScottyBro over a separate site or a local link. Matches the life-OS direction (Orbit owns people) while the rebuild is designed.

statement: Every form in the admin sits behind a button, in a modal.
choice: Pages show a button that opens FormModal (components/ui): dialog semantics, focus in/out, Esc, submit on Enter, busy lock, errors shown in the modal with the typed values kept; bottom sheet on phones. Inline create/edit forms across the app are converted. Search, filters, toggles, segmented controls and the chat input are controls, not forms, and stay on the page.
rationale: Scott, 2026-09-17: 'everything in heyscottybro if its a form must be behind a modal and button, there can be no forms out on the page, it looks too unprofessional.'

statement: Achilles is heyScottyBro's Health space, not a separate app (narrows DR-015).
choice: /admin/health with tabs Overview, Workouts, Food, Body, plus a live workout at /admin/health/workout/:id. Food, body weight and targets reuse food_logs, weight_logs and nutrition_profiles (one profile per user, unique index); new tables workout_plans, workout_sessions (one open at a time) and workout_sets (weight_lb) carry plans and live sets, and the old flat `workouts` rows were imported as sessions. Weights are suggested by double progression in src/utils/overload.js (hit the top of the rep range on every set -> add 5 lb, or 2.5 under 20 lb; short of the range three sessions running -> 10% deload), insights are computed in src/utils/healthInsights.js and the AI coach only ever sees those computed numbers. Workouts are built by hand or from an AI prompt (claude-sonnet-4-6, reviewed before saving); food can be estimated by AI (haiku) before saving. Frodo gets log_food and log_weight plus read-only food_log, body_weight and workout_sets. Built inside this repo (no new Vercel function: the Hobby plan is at its 12-function limit).
rationale: Scott, 2026-09-17: 'add in achilles, my health page… tracking calories and weight, and workouts… built based on an ai prompt or me manually doing it… whenever I do a set I log how many reps I did, of that set and what weight, the weight should be set for me already based on my past tracked records, and progressive overload… give me insights to improve.' DR-015 moved these domains out to a separate app; he asked for them here instead, so the data never left.
